cards.front: How do you find the perimeter of a rectangle?
cards.back: Add all four sides, or work out 2 × (length + width).
cards.say: How do you find the perimeter of a rectangle? Add all four sides, or work out two times (length plus width).

cards.front: How do you find the area of a rectangle?
cards.back: Multiply the length by the width.
cards.say: How do you find the area of a rectangle? Multiply the length by the width.

cards.front: A rectangle is 12 m long and 5 m wide. What is its area?
cards.say: A rectangle is twelve metres long and five metres wide. What is its area? Sixty square metres. Twelve times five equals sixty.

cards.front: A rectangle is 12 m long and 5 m wide. What is its perimeter?
cards.say: A rectangle is twelve metres long and five metres wide. What is its perimeter? Thirty four metres. Two times (twelve plus five) equals two times seventeen equals thirty four.

cards.front: A room is 9 m long and 4 m wide. What area of carpet covers the floor?
cards.say: A room is nine metres long and four metres wide. What area of carpet covers the floor? Thirty six square metres. Nine times four equals thirty six.

cards.front: A garden is 15 m long and 10 m wide. How long is the fence around it?
cards.say: A garden is fifteen metres long and ten metres wide. How long is the fence around it? Fifty metres. Two times (fifteen plus ten) equals fifty.

cards.front: A square has a perimeter of 36 cm. How long is each side?
cards.say: A square has a perimeter of thirty six centimetres. How long is each side? Nine centimetres. Thirty six divided by four equals nine.

cards.front: A rectangle has an area of 48 cm² and a width of 6 cm. How long is it?
cards.say: A rectangle has an area of forty eight square centimetres and a width of six centimetres. How long is it? Eight centimetres. Forty eight divided by six equals eight.

cards.front: A rectangle has a perimeter of 30 cm and a length of 9 cm. What is its width?
cards.back:
6 cm
Two lengths make 18, so two widths make 12, and one width is 6.
cards.say: A rectangle has a perimeter of thirty centimetres and a length of nine centimetres. What is its width? Six centimetres. Two lengths make eighteen, so two widths make twelve, and one width is six.

cards.front: A shape joins a 6 cm by 4 cm rectangle and a 3 cm by 2 cm rectangle, with no overlap. What is its total area?
cards.say: A shape joins a rectangle six by four centimetres and a rectangle three by two centimetres, with no overlap. What is its total area? Thirty square centimetres.

cards.front: A 10 cm by 6 cm rectangle has a 4 cm by 3 cm rectangle cut out. What area is left?
cards.say: A rectangle ten by six centimetres has a rectangle four by three centimetres cut out. What area is left? Forty eight square centimetres. Sixty take away twelve.

cards.front: Two rectangles have a perimeter of 16 cm: 6 cm by 2 cm, and 4 cm by 4 cm. Which has the bigger area?
cards.back:
The 4 cm by 4 cm one.
4 × 4 = 16 cm² and 6 × 2 = 12 cm².
cards.say: Two rectangles have a perimeter of sixteen centimetres: six by two, and four by four. Which has the bigger area? The four by four one. Sixteen beats twelve.

cards.front: A regular octagon has sides of 5 cm. What is its perimeter?
cards.say: A regular octagon has sides of five centimetres. What is its perimeter? Forty centimetres. Eight times five equals forty.

cards.front: An equilateral triangle has a perimeter of 27 cm. How long is each side?
cards.say: An equilateral triangle has a perimeter of twenty seven centimetres. How long is each side? Nine centimetres. Twenty seven divided by three equals nine.

cards.front: A square has an area of 49 cm². What is its perimeter?
cards.back:
28 cm
The side is 7 cm, because 7 × 7 = 49. Then 4 × 7 = 28.
cards.say: A square has an area of forty nine square centimetres. What is its perimeter? Twenty eight centimetres. The side is seven, and four times seven is twenty eight.

cards.front: A rectangle is 20 cm long and 3 cm wide. What is its area?
cards.say: A rectangle is twenty centimetres long and three centimetres wide. What is its area? Sixty square centimetres. Twenty times three equals sixty.

cards.front: A rectangle is 20 cm long and 3 cm wide. What is its perimeter?
cards.say: A rectangle is twenty centimetres long and three centimetres wide. What is its perimeter? Forty six centimetres. Two times (twenty plus three) equals forty six.

cards.front: A square playground has sides of 8 m. What is its area?
cards.say: A square playground has sides of eight metres. What is its area? Sixty four square metres. Eight times eight equals sixty four.

cards.front: A pool is 25 m long and 4 m wide. What is its area?
cards.say: A pool is twenty five metres long and four metres wide. What is its area? One hundred square metres. Twenty five times four equals one hundred.

cards.front: A pool is 25 m long and 4 m wide. What is its perimeter?
cards.say: A pool is twenty five metres long and four metres wide. What is its perimeter? Fifty eight metres. Two times (twenty five plus four) equals fifty eight.

cards.front: A floor is 6 m by 5 m. How many 1 m by 1 m tiles cover it?
cards.say: A floor is six metres by five metres. How many one metre by one metre tiles cover it? Thirty tiles. Six times five equals thirty.

cards.front: A rectangle is 1 cm wide and 12 cm long. What is its perimeter?
cards.say: A rectangle is one centimetre wide and twelve centimetres long. What is its perimeter? Twenty six centimetres. Two times (twelve plus one) equals twenty six.

cards.front: Which unit do we use for area: cm, cm² or kg?
cards.say: Which unit do we use for area: centimetres, square centimetres or kilograms? Square centimetres.
